arxiv-2605-10000: Diamond membranes serve as a platform for photonic and opto-mechanical applications — quantum light on diamond. plos-pone-0003400: Computer scientists built ANGLOR, a shape-predicting tool, in this 2008 bioinformatics paper. plos-pone-0003500: Theorists Zanotto and Krakauer read viral genomes as co-evolving systems in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003600: Ophthalmic geneticists hunted inflammation genes behind blinding trachoma in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003700: In 2008, Mooers, Faith, and Maddison turned red-list labels into extinction odds. plos-pone-0003800: Lietha and Eck solved a cancer target caught with its inhibitor in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003900: Working in 2008, Malone and Fontenot studied how toads split into species. Analyzing patterns of reproductive isolation across toad groups, they probed speciation's general rules. The toad data test which barriers matter most when one lineage becomes two.
plos-pone-0004000: In 2008, Kweku, Liu, and Adjuik tested seasonal malaria prevention in Ghanaian children. plos-pone-0004100: In 2008, Long, Renzette, and Centore compared two live bacterial mutants. Two recA mutants showed uneven needs for constant SOS expression in E. coli. The repair protein's variants diverged in switching on the alarm. The contrast sharpens the SOS circuit map.
plos-pone-0004200: In 2009, Wang, Liu, and Tao dealt genes like cards in mice. Their STARS method set precise odds for switching genes on or off cleanly. Regulated sparseness let users dial activation probability. The genetic dice bring control to mosaic mouse experiments.
plos-pone-0004300: In 2009, Wagner, Smolka, and de Bruin mapped a cell-cycle brake's fine controls. Whi5 regulation by site-specific CDK phosphorylation was fully charted in yeast. The repressor's off-switch was mapped phosphate by tiny phosphate. The neat map clarifies the G1/S transition nicely.
plos-pone-0357100: Sponge cities absorb rain like a sponge instead of flooding — but that depends on the soil. This paper mapped the spatial variability of soil texture using fractal dimensions, then applied the results to sponge city construction. The method tells urban planners where the ground will drink and where it will drown.
plos-pone-0358700: When a self-driving car hands control back to the human, is the human ready? This review surveyed driver state detection and recognition for conditional automated driving. plos-pone-0356800: Eribulin fights advanced breast cancer — but real-world safety data matters beyond clinical trials. plos-pone-0358600: Gas fields can carry natural radioactivity to the surface with the fuel. plos-pone-0357900: Farmworkers face repeated pesticide exposure — and muscles and nerves may pay the price. plos-pone-0352900: Grant peer review may carry hidden gender and disciplinary biases that warp who gets funded. plos-pone-0357000: Factory maintenance must balance production demands against breakdown risks — under uncertainty. The mathematics optimizes the wrench schedule for maximum output at minimum risk.
plos-pone-0357500: Announcing an upcoming test changes how language learners use subtitles. This paper studied the impact of test announcements on subtitle reliance and video comprehension, examining the roles of vocabulary size and working memory. The findings help teachers use — or withhold — subtitles strategically.
plos-pone-0356200: Online games bleed players constantly — and predicting who quits next is big business. plos-pone-0354800: Ghanaians choose between types of primary health care facilities — but what drives the choice? The findings tell health planners what patients actually value — distance, quality, cost — so resources can follow real demand.
plos-pone-0354700: Predicting trauma survival accurately guides the most urgent medical decisions. plos-pone-0355600: HIV patients with uncontrolled viremia need new therapeutic targets. plos-pone-0356100: Do blood triglycerides cause endometriosis — or merely accompany it? plos-pone-0356000: Antipsychotics cause adverse drug reactions that go underreported in Africa. plos-pone-0355200: The atherogenic index of plasma — a simple lipid ratio — might flag older adults at risk of diabetic kidney disease. plos-pone-0355400: Missing data has patterns — and seeing them prevents bad analysis. This paper presented a visual analytic method for investigating patterns and structures of missingness. plos-pone-0354900: Queues with retrials, re-service, balking, and working vacations — the messy reality of service systems — need rigorous models. plos-pone-0355300: Stroke striking the young in the UAE — an alarming trend — needed documentation. This single-center retrospective analysis examined risk factors and outcomes of young-onset stroke. The findings expose what’s driving strokes in young Emiratis — essential for prevention.
plos-pone-0351400: Suburban women’s health-promoting lifestyles — shaped by class, culture, and place — deserve critical ethnographic study. This paper published the protocol for exactly that. europmc-pmc2791200: Snakebite gets little attention from drug companies and global health funders, and this 2009 paper argues that is exactly why it is a disease of poverty. europmc-pmc2847200: Bacterial biofilms are fortresses, and this 2010 paper reveals one of their building tricks. europmc-pmc2910600: Friends may be as vital as diet. This 2010 meta-analysis finds social relationships strongly predict mortality risk. The authors pool 148 studies covering 300,000 people. Their result puts loneliness on par with smoking. The paper made social connection a public health issue.
europmc-pmc2928800: Germs wield protein spearguns with different jobs. This 2010 paper shows Burkholderia's type VI firing systems play split roles against animal cells versus rival germs. europmc-pmc2948500: Colon tumors speak in gene signals, and this 2010 paper listens with care. The authors chart cancer-driving signals in colon tumors with many-sided chip tests built for trust. europmc-pmc3043000: Liver clocks tick on BMAL1 rhythms. This 2011 paper maps where the BMAL1 clock protein grips DNA across the day in mouse liver. The authors reveal the clock's grip. Their work lights up body-clock science. Thousands of liver genes dance to the beat.
europmc-pmc6528300: Chloroplast genomes - plastomes - hold key clues to plant evolution, but annotating their genes by hand is slow. europmc-pmc6651100: Essential oils owe much of their germ-killing power to terpenes and terpenoids - fragrant plant chemicals. europmc-pmc6728300: When chronic liver disease suddenly crashes, it becomes acute-on-chronic liver failure - and definitions varied by region.
